subject.title: fix(azure): responses model aliases route correctly

question: Should endpoint-bearing manifest/config surface be the generic authority for retaining Azure Responses provider ownership, with the supplied mock probe accepted as sufficient routing proof?
rationale: The implementation is internally consistent, but this choice defines an auth-provider ownership boundary and determines whether a local mock is enough evidence for a credential-routing regression.

options.title: Accept after green checks
options.body: Accept the endpoint-surface ownership rule and mock routing proof once all exact-head required checks pass.

options.title: Require live Azure proof
options.body: Hold merge until a redacted real Azure account probe confirms provider, URL, header, and successful credential exchange.

options.title: Move policy to provider hook
options.body: Request a narrower OpenAI plugin-owned transport or normalization hook if the alias rule should not become generic core behavior.

recommendation.title: Accept after green checks
recommendation.body: Accept the endpoint-surface ownership rule and mock routing proof once all exact-head required checks pass.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work most directly overlaps provider ownership, unknown-model guidance, suppression, and runtime fallback behavior.
